turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:

I've lived there for quite some time, you see, and as a management analyst, my entire career has been built on identifying patterns, anomalies, structural inefficiencies, and behavioral trends... so I know a pattern when I see one. I don't just jump to conclusions. But for months now—specifically starting around late October, though the preamble was likely earlier—the property manager, in direct collusion with certain specific individuals in the building, has been employing these incredibly specific, calculated tactics to pressure me into vacating the premises. 

It started with the mail. Misdelivered mail. And I don't mean a random grocery flyer, Doctor. I mean my important documents, intentionally routed to the wrong boxes or left slightly torn on the mailroom table, just to send a message that my privacy is compromised. Then came the noises. Now, they will tell you it's an old building, but these aren't settling pipes or standard acoustic bleed. They are timed noises in the walls. Rhythmic thumping, specifically calibrated to my schedule, usually starting exactly fourteen minutes after I turn off my bedside lamp, or the moment I sit down at my desk to review my files. 

And the neighbors... they make these little comments in the hallway or the elevator. Passing remarks about "people overstaying their welcome" or "time for a change of scenery," always delivered with this very specific cadence, looking right at me. The property management office keeps sending me these memos, these boilerplate explanations about USPS carrier errors or HVAC maintenance, and they wave all this paperwork in my face. But no amount of their fabricated documentation or patronizing explanations changes the undeniable, empirical pattern I can see with my own two eyes. It is a textbook, orchestrated pressure campaign, and frankly, it takes a massive amount of my time just to properly document it all.
